clue.text: No longer taking part — may be in touch

definitions.meaning: a player out of the game, no longer involved
a ball that has gone into touch, over the sideline in rugby or football, is dead

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both someone removed from the action and a ball beyond the field's boundary.

clue.text: Different dam, miles away

indicators.note: away tells us the miles abbreviation is sent off from the word

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A reservoir wall somewhere far off is unlike the local one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' looks like a reservoir wall but is the farming word for a mother animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something other is distinct or not the same, hence different.

clue.text: Grew rich, originally hero in dire TV programme

indicators.note: in tells us the hero's initial goes inside the rearranged letters
programme here means arrange or set out anew, so the words dire and TV are reordered
originally points to the opening letter of the word hero

explanation.surface: Someone made a fortune, having first played the hero in a terrible television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'programme' is used as a verb, to arrange anew; 'in dire TV programme' reads as a single bad show, hiding the split.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive is to prosper or flourish, so grew rich fits the past form.

clue.text: One used to cook breakfast, or woke lacking energy?

definitions.text: One used to cook breakfast, or woke lacking energy?

parts.words: One used to cook breakfast, or woke lacking energy?
parts.note: a kitchen utensil for bacon and eggs; and take E (energy) away from woke to leave the name of another such vessel, the Chinese wok

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a riddle: woke without its E is WOK, a pan, steering you to the same kind of object.
explanation.definitionFit: This shallow pan is the classic utensil for cooking a fried breakfast.

clue.text: Taking the credit for track record

definitions.text: Taking the credit for track record

parts.words: Taking the credit for track record
parts.note: an athlete who has set a record circles the track to accept the crowd's applause

explanation.definitionFit: A celebratory circuit run by a winner to acknowledge acclaim is exactly taking credit on the track.

clue.text: Meet up and gossip -

indicators.note: in a down entry, up tells us the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Friends get together for a chat, a sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue and 6 Down read as one sentence, the dash joining them; 'Meet' is the money sense, settling a cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To yap is to chatter or talk idly, much as gossips do.

clue.text: Embraced by Darcy, Lizzie recalled clinging fabric

indicators.note: recalled, called back, tells us the run of letters is taken in reverse order
embraced by tells us the letters are held within the words Darcy, Lizzie

explanation.surface: In a Pride and Prejudice scene, Elizabeth remembers the tight dress she wore when Mr Darcy hugged her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embraced by' picks ARCYL from inside 'Darcy, Lizzie' and 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is an elastic synthetic material that fits tightly to the body.

clue.text: — just look at the state of the neighbourhood!

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
Cal is an abbreviation for the US state of California

explanation.surface: The sentence from 5 Down ends in a complaint about how run-down the area has become.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 5 Down; 'just' and 'at the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A local shop or matter belongs to the nearby area, the immediate surroundings.

clue.text: Race about nursing the man, being fantastic

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one piece is held inside the other
about here means in a jumble, so the letters of race are rearranged

parts.note: him is the pronoun for the man

explanation.surface: A racer looking after a man is doing something marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being fantastic' reads as an adjective phrase but is a noun: a fantastic being, a creature of myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a mythical monster with parts of several animals, so a fantastic being.

clue.text: Emerge having grasped everything to refute a philosopher

indicators.note: having grasped tells us the first word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to emerge is to arise or come up

indicators.note: to refute, to reject, tells us the letter a is thrown out of the word

parts.note: the total is everything, the whole amount
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stands up having understood the whole argument, ready to rebut a great thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refute' does double duty in the surface as rebut, but here it simply means reject, so the single letter is thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Plato, one of the great figures of philosophy.

clue.text: Be quick with hot, spicy food, about to go to town

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: to go tells us a letter departs from the word

parts.note: curry is a spicy dish
C is short for circa, Latin for about
up means towards town or the capital, as in going up to London

explanation.surface: A diner is told to get a move on with a takeaway before heading into town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to go' strips C (circa) from CURRY; going 'up' to town is the British habit of speaking of travel to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurry up is an imperative urging someone to move fast.

clue.text: Opera producer disappearing outside, hiccuping uncontrollably

indicators.note: uncontrollably suggests letters let loose and thrown into a new order
disappearing outside means the word's outer letters vanish, leaving its interior

explanation.surface: A theatre impresario fades from view outdoors while suffering a fit of hiccups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disappearing outside' loses the first and last letters of 'hiccuping', leaving ICCUPIN, which 'uncontrollably' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Puccini composed operas such as La Boheme and Tosca, so he produced operas.

clue.text: Head off yellow bird

indicators.note: head off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, as does craven

explanation.surface: A command to intercept a yellow bird before it escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' looks like the bird's colour, but it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Most awkward part of orchestration — one kept in time

indicators.note: kept in tells us one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: fiddles, the violins, are a section of an orchestra
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The hardest passage of the score is the one the player keeps in tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' puts I inside FIDDLES, giving FIDDLIES, then T for time follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddly means tricky and awkward to handle, and this is its superlative.

clue.text: Deceive Lorraine, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the Cross of Lorraine has two crossbars

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means betray, and the Lorraine cross is an example of a two-barred cross.

clue.text: Leather worn to tease

definitions.meaning: a soft leather made from young goat skin, as in gloves
to josh or rib someone playfully

explanation.definitionFit: The word names goatskin leather and also means to joke with someone.

clue.text: Gives up sweet stuff, given sudden impetus

parts.note: to kick a habit is to give it up
a tart is a sweet pastry

explanation.surface: Someone renounces sugary food and suddenly finds new energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives up' is the habit-quitting sense; 'given' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost that gets something going abruptly, like starting a motorbike with a kick.

clue.text: Sticking out in favour of underground rave

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
the Tube is the London Underground railway
to rave is to rant wildly

explanation.surface: Someone supports a party held down in the subway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground rave' suggests an illegal party, but it splits into the London railway and a tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Protuberant means bulging or projecting from a surface.

clue.text: Type of mortgage one's landed with?

definitions.meaning: a home loan repaid from a maturing investment policy
a gift or bequest settled on someone, here punningly property bestowed

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a mortgage linked to an investment policy and a gift of funds or property.

clue.text: Dismissed for failing to meet delivery?

definitions.text: Dismissed for failing to meet delivery?

parts.words: Dismissed for failing to meet delivery?
parts.note: in cricket a batsman out when he misses the ball and it hits the stumps

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler's ball is a 'delivery'; missing it so it strikes the wicket is a dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman is out this way when the ball beats the bat and hits the stumps directly.

clue.text: Occasional coverage The Sun has provided

definitions.text: Occasional coverage The Sun has provided

parts.words: Occasional coverage The Sun has provided
parts.note: reads like a tabloid's reporting, but describes the Sun being covered up by the Moon from time to time

explanation.walkthrough: The italic 'The Sun' suggests the British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar blackout happens when the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun, an occasional covering.

clue.text: Rod given signal to come on

definitions.meaning: the stick used in snooker or billiards
an actor's prompt to enter the stage

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a billiard stick and a theatrical prompt for an entrance.

clue.text: Murderer interrupted by fit officer

indicators.note: interrupted by tells us the second word breaks into the first

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in the Bible
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A killer is stopped by a muscular policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like 'athletic' but means suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a commissioned rank in army and navy.

clue.text: Eating out, perhaps, I push curl out of the way

indicators.note: out of the way means displaced, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone dining out brushes a stray curl aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating' is corrosive: this acid eats away metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulphuric acid is highly corrosive, so it eats away at materials.

clue.text: Give a lift to one in the army

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a host is an army or large multitude
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Offer a ride to a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Host is the old sense of an army, as in the heavenly host.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise up, to give a lift literally.

clue.text: Window-cleaner seeing someone drying off?

definitions.meaning: the blade that clears a windscreen
one who rubs things dry, like a towel user

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a car's screen blade and one who rubs something dry.

clue.text: Current right-hand person?

parts.note: R and H abbreviate right and hand
one means a person, as in one would think

explanation.surface: Asking about one's present trusted assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is the noun: a river flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major river of Switzerland and France, a flowing body of water.

clue.text: Get the post sorted

parts.note: sounds like handling the mail, but means filling a job

explanation.definitionFit: To name someone to a job is to fill the position.

clue.text: Knock when the postman turns up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turns up tells us the name is written upwards

parts.note: Postman Pat is the British children's TV postman

explanation.surface: A rap at the door as the mail arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a British children's TV character, a village postman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap is a light knock.

clue.text: Heart possibly retains energy with old herbal preparation

indicators.note: retains means keeps within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the heart is an example of a bodily organ
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A traditional herbal remedy is said to keep the heart vigorous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retains' puts E inside ORGAN; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a dried culinary herb used in seasoning.

clue.text: Crime article paper published

parts.note: the is the definite article
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A crime story appears in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'published' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Timing right for cut, maybe, but never slice

definitions.text: Timing right for cut, maybe, but never slice

parts.words: Timing right for cut, maybe, but never slice
parts.note: grammar: the verb cut keeps its form for things gone by, but slice must change

explanation.walkthrough: Cut has the same form for yesterday as today; slice becomes sliced, so the form does not suit it unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: This grammatical form expresses action completed earlier, as with cut for yesterday.
